images.author: James Steakley
images.caption: The Richard C. Smith House in Jefferson, Wisconsin, is a Usonian house designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.  It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

brief: Frank Lloyd Wright Usonian house of 1950: low walls of stacked, ragged-coursed limestone and wood under a flat roof with a broad cantilevered overhang, a stone chimney mass, a brick-red concrete walk to a recessed entrance and a big lawn.

facade.notes: the Richard C. Smith House (Jefferson WI, 1950): long walls of layered local limestone under a very low-pitched roof with deep eaves and a cypress fascia, a red-tinted concrete walk to a recessed entry, a carport; under a big oak; an unshorn lawn

why.note: a Wright Usonian: low roofs, local materials, the house turned to its garden
Wright laid local stone in thin courses like the bedrock it came from
